entries.reason: the release carries the class itself, so there is nothing to carry: it arrived in iOS 4.0, the band floor of this library is 6.0, and a backport that defined it would put a second class of that name on the release that owns it. Measured at the floor: the AVFoundation image of the armv7 cache of 6.1.3, extracted with modules/apple/dyld.lua extract(), exports _OBJC_CLASS_$_AVCompositionTrack and _OBJC_METACLASS_$_AVCompositionTrack, and the armv7 class table of 6.0 gives the class 6 own instance methods - _initWithAsset:trackID:trackIndex:, _mutableComposition, segments, dealloc, description and finalize - above AVAssetTrack's 52, with AVMovie nowhere in that image at all. What the port has to say about this class is the 13.0 members it does not carry, and those are the absent rows beside this one: AVCompositionTrack.formatDescriptionReplacements and -[AVCompositionTrack associatedTracksOfType:]
entries.effect: the class is the release's own and does what it does there: NSClassFromString answers AVCompositionTrack, -segments and -segmentForTrackTime: answer as they do on 6.1.3, and the port adds nothing to the class and changes nothing about it. A caller that wants to know what a composition track carries asks -[AVAssetTrack formatDescriptions] and -segments, which is what the release itself offers
entries.source: the class symbol and its metaclass in the AVFoundation image of ~/.charon/dyld/6.1.3/dyld_shared_cache_armv7, extracted with modules/apple/dyld.lua extract() and read through that image's own symbol table; the 6 own instance methods and the superclass from the armv7 class table of 6.0, ~/.charon/dyld/6.0/classes_armv7.json, where the class is CARRIED by AVFoundation.framework and AVMovie is ABSENT; ios(4.0) for the class's own availability from the iPhoneOS 16.4 SDK, AVFoundation/AVCompositionTrack.h:32

entries.reason: the release carries the class itself, so there is nothing to carry: it arrived in iOS 4.0 beside AVCompositionTrack, the band floor of this library is 6.0, and the release's own is the one a caller gets. Measured at the floor: the AVFoundation image of the armv7 cache of 6.1.3 exports _OBJC_CLASS_$_AVMutableCompositionTrack and its metaclass, and the armv7 class table of 6.0 gives the class 19 own instance methods above AVCompositionTrack's 6 - insertTimeRange:ofTrack:atTime:error:, insertTimeRanges:ofTracks:atTime:error:, insertEmptyTimeRange:, removeTimeRange:, segments and scaleTimeRange:toDuration: among them. The 13.0 member the port is asked about is the absent row beside this one, -[AVMutableCompositionTrack replaceFormatDescription:withFormatDescription:], which 6.1.3's own 19 selectors do not include
entries.effect: the class is the release's own and does what it does there: -insertTimeRange:ofTrack:atTime:error:, -removeTimeRange: and -scaleTimeRange:toDuration: edit a track as they do on 6.1.3, which is the whole of the track editing this release does, and the port defines no class of its own here. A caller exports the composition it edited
